criteria.rationale: Verified that review dispatch sets POSE_SEALED_CHECKOUT to the worktree and that IsSealedCheckout resolves absolute paths and symlinks before comparing the CLI root. Store writers use the same predicate. L1 is the disclosed residual assumption: a reviewer process that clears the environment marker can write, while dispatch’s post-run comparison still invalidates a changed checkout. This is the spec’s explicit residual risk.

The change adds no goroutines, shared mutable state or asynchronous lifecycle. Persistence is decided per command invocation and writer guards execute synchronously. No new cancellation surface is introduced; focused assessment and review-plan tests passed.

Reviewed the additive --no-persist CLI option, help text, and review-plan command arguments. The three assessment commands marshal the same result objects to JSON; persisted file formats are unchanged. The brief template advances to review-brief/9 for its new instruction.

The new option is a boolean and introduces no unbounded input. Sealed write attempts through init, snapshot and request return an actionable refusal. Store writers return ErrSealedAssessmentWrite with --no-persist remediation. Regression coverage exercises sealed commands with --update-state and --no-persist.

Traced CLI assessment calls into guarded Store writers and review-plan generation into dispatched command arguments. No REST, event, MCP schema or cross-service contract changes. The live integration assessment reported three unobserved HTTP contracts unrelated to this change.
Non-persisting commands emit a stderr hint while keeping result JSON on stdout. Refused writes return a typed error with usable remediation, and save/update-state failures retain command context.

Examined the CLI, review-plan arguments, help catalog and review-brief template versioning. --no-persist is additive; absent it, persistence remains enabled outside sealed checkouts. Existing assessment records and indexes keep their formats and meaning.

Focused go -C pose-mcp test ./internal/cli ./internal/pose -run 'Assess|ReviewPlanRunsAssessments' and scoped vet passed. The regression test hashes the fixture tree around each writing assessment route, checks refusal routes and verifies normal persistence outside sealed checkout. Full validators were blocked before Go checks could execute by read-only temp/cache paths; sealed validation evidence passes.

The failure cause is assessment commands persisting derived files into the reviewer’s sealed worktree. D1 addresses it at both layers: CLI skips writes and preserves result output, while Store writers refuse as a last line. D2 makes review plans explicitly choose --no-persist. The design assessment observed no material structural deltas, so no structural facts require mappings.

Compared runtime flags and review-brief/9 instructions with CLI help, POSE.md, the pt-BR manual and both scaffold copies. They consistently describe dispatching-engine invocation and no-persist behavior.

A reviewer can tell results were not persisted from the stderr hint. Direct write attempts explain that the checkout is sealed and identify --no-persist as remediation; command failures identify the writer or update-state operation.

R1 is covered by no-persist output/no-write tests; R2 by unchanged-tree and refusal tests; R3 by reviewToolArgs tests; R4 by before/after tree digest regression; R5 by the review-brief/9 instruction and current-brief regression. The focused test command passed.

The implementation covers the specified pose-mcp CLI, Store writers, planned assessment arguments and operational documentation. It does not change assessment scoring or data formats. The design assessment reported no material structural deltas, and surface-check found one target with zero findings.

The new environmental authority is the dispatch-provided checkout path; matching canonicalizes absolute and symlink paths. Every assessment Store writer is guarded, while the CLI prevents capability-artifact writes. No new dependency, secret, external execution authority or user-controlled output path is introduced. Marker-clearing residual is disclosed as L1.

The layered policy is the smallest sufficient design for both behaviors: a CLI-only check leaves other Store callers able to write, while a Store-only refusal makes planned review commands fail instead of returning results. Explicit plan flags also work when commands are copied into another checkout. No new schema or cache is added. The choice would need revisiting if dispatch stopped setting the marker or new writers bypassed the guard; post-run checkout comparison and writer regression coverage address those cases.
